messages:
incident-bot: Pager — P1: GPU provisioning backlog spiking on cluster infer-eu-west. 5m avg pending pods = 428. Affected nodepool: gpu-pool-eu. Runbook: https://runbook.internal/infra/gpu-autoscale

sarah (oncall): ack, looking. I see queue growth on the inference-serve deployment. Investigating autoscaler events now.

sarah (oncall): kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-serve
```
NAME               REFERENCE            TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
inference-serve    Deployment/inference  100%/80%  2         10        2
```

len (eng-runtime): copying autoscaler logs, there's a recurring error when attempting scale-up:
```
I0212 14:02:31 cluster.go:567] ScaleUp: failed to create node: Error creating launch template version: InvalidLaunchTemplateId.NotFound: The launch template ID 'lt-0abcde12345' does not exist
```

omar (eng-sre): that matches what we saw in staging yesterday. Looks like an automated launch-template promotion removed the version the ASG references. If ASG points to a non-existent LT version, ASG scaling attempts will fail.

priya (eng-infra): confirmation: AWS describe-auto-scaling-groups shows DesiredCapacity attempts but InstanceIds not created. Also seeing "CreateFleet error: iam:PassRole denied" for one of the older LT versions in cloudtrail. Could be a combined IAM + LT mismatch.

sarah (oncall): trying manual scale to buy time: 
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-eu --desired-capacity 4 --no-honor-cooldown
```
Result: 
```
Error: Could not launch new instance: InvalidLaunchTemplateId.NotFound: Launch template version not found for LaunchTemplateId: lt-0abcde12345
```

omar (eng-sre): immediate mitigation options:
- recreate a temporary LT version with the correct instance profile + sg, point ASG to it (fast but risky), OR
- create a separate emergency ASG (gpu-pool-eu-emergency) with a known-good LT and attach to cluster (safer - avoids touching live ASG), OR
- fallback to CPU-only pool (degrades latency) while infra is fixed.

priya (eng-infra): I'm starting an emergency LT version now with the same template data pulled from the last known-good snapshot. Will add correct instance profile (role: rwd-gpu-instance-role) and required lifecycle hooks. Pushing new LT version -> lt-0f1e2d3c4b.

deploy-bot: Deploy started for infra/emergency-lt @priya. CI job 5123 in progress.

len (eng-runtime): autoscaler still retrying; once LT exists the autoscaler should succeed. Keep an eye on kubelet registration.

priya (eng-infra): LT created and published as version 6 (lt-0f1e2d3c4b). Updating ASG launch template to use version 6 now.

sarah (oncall): running manual desired-capacity again to 6.
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-eu --desired-capacity 6 --no-honor-cooldown
```
Result: Accepted. ASG launching 4 instances.

(some time passes)

deploy-bot: New instances launching: i-0aa11bb22cc33dd44, i-0ee55ff66gg77hh88.

omar (eng-sre): nodes joined cluster: 
```
kubectl get nodes | grep gpu
ip-192-168-10-12   Ready  gpu=true  3d
ip-192-168-10-13   Ready  gpu=true  2h
```

sarah (oncall): inference backlog dropped from 428 -> 12 over 8 minutes. Throttle cleared.

maya (support): support notes: we saw ~15 customer threads referencing slow API responses between 14:00-14:22 CET. Customers impacted mostly on eu-west. Logged incident refs: CS-8421, CS-8423. Notifying top-20 customers via standard template.

len (eng-runtime): post-mortem notes in brief: root cause appears to be a manual automation job that deleted an unused LT version, but the ASG was implicitly referencing that version due to a previous patch. Also a regression in infra deploy tooling that didn't update ASG references atomically.

priya (eng-infra): action items (short):
- re-run audit of ASG->LaunchTemplate references across all clusters (priority).
- add validation to infra deploys to prevent deletion of LT versions currently referenced by ASGs.
- add autoscaler retry/backoff improvements to surface LT-not-found earlier in alerts.
- create a self-healing playbook to create emergency LT versions from snapshots.

sarah (oncall): severity downgraded to P2. Will open incident doc and invite eng-infra and eng-sre for a follow-up at 16:00 CET. Assigning follow-ups to priya/omar/len.

omar (eng-sre): handing off monitoring to sarah->omar for next shift. omar will be primary owner for postmortem.

sarah (oncall): handing incident to omar (02:00-10:00 UTC oncall). Key checklist for next owner:
- confirm no ASGs referencing deleted LT versions remain
- verify instance profile permissions (iam:PassRole) on LT versions
- review deploy pipeline that prunes LT versions
- correlate customer errors and update CS tickets with timeline

omar (eng-sre): ack, I'll take it. Adding this to #incidents-summary and starting the incident page: https://incidents.internal/1923456789

maya (support): I'll follow up with CS to confirm customers got the update and close the immediate tickets.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> P2 transition recorded. Duration (P1): ~22m.

sarah (oncall): TL;DR — autoscaler failures due to ASG referencing deleted LT version + occasional IAM passrole denial. Manual emergency LT created and ASG updated; backlog cleared. Postmortem + infra fixes scheduled.
